en.headline: Central Government approves removal of housing chief Winnie Ho
en.dek: The State Council accepted Chief Executive John Lee’s recommendation on Tuesday, formalising Ho’s departure after she resigned over the Tai Po fire.
body: The Central People’s Government has approved the removal of Winnie Ho Wing-yin from her post as Secretary for Housing, the Hong Kong government said on Monday.

The decision follows a recommendation by Chief Executive John Lee, made in accordance with the Basic Law after Ho tendered her resignation last Wednesday to assume political accountability for the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po.

In a statement, Lee noted that Ho had joined the government in 1992, served as Director of Architectural Services from 2020, and became Secretary for Housing in 2022. He commended her work on Light Public Housing construction and efforts to shorten the waiting time for subsidised rental housing.
Lee said Ho’s duty was suspended with effect from her resignation and that Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong had taken up the acting role. He wished her well as she left office on Tuesday.

zh.headline: 中央政府批准免去何永賢房屋局局長職務
zh.dek: 國務院周二根據行政長官李家超建議正式免職，何永賢早前因大埔宏福苑火災請辭承擔政治責任。
body: 香港政府周一表示，中央人民政府已批准免去何永賢的房屋局局長職務。
有關決定是根據《基本法》規定，按行政長官李家超的建議作出。何永賢上周三提出請辭，願意為大埔宏福苑火災承擔政治責任。
李家超在聲明中指出，何永賢1992年加入政府，2020年起出任建築署署長，2022年獲任命為房屋局局長。他讚揚她在興建簡約公屋及縮短公屋輪候時間方面的工作。
李家超表示，何永賢請辭當日起職務已暫停，由財政司副司長黃偉綸兼任署理。他祝願她離任後事事順遂。
